subproblem.title: Lemma T: limits of singular points are singular for the weak limit
subproblem.statement: Let P, n, Q ∈ ℕ, let F be a set of functions ℝ^P → ℝ^Q and let sing map functions ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to subsets of ℝ^P. Write φ_k ⇀ φ if ∫ f·φ_k dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ dμH[n] for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume (A.3c) sing φ is closed for every φ ∈ F, and (A.3(3)) whenever φ ∈ F, φ_k ∈ F and φ_k ⇀ φ, for every ε > 0 there is k₀ with B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k ⊆ {x : ∃ z ∈ sing φ, |x − z| < ε} for all k ≥ k₀. If ψ ∈ F, φ_k ∈ F for all k, φ_k ⇀ ψ, z_k ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k for every k and z_k → z, then z ∈ sing ψ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n Q : ℕ) (F : Set (Euclid P → Euclid Q)) (sing : (Euclid P → Euclid Q) → Set (Euclid P)), (∀ φ ∈ F, IsClosed (sing φ)) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ φs : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid Q, (∀ k, φs k ∈ F) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • φs k x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • φ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, ball (0 : Euclid P) 1 ∩ sing (φs k) ⊆ {x | ∃ z ∈ sing φ, dist x z < ε}) → ∀ ψ ∈ F, ∀ φs : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid Q, (∀ k, φs k ∈ F) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • φs k x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • ψ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))) → ∀ (zs : ℕ → Euclid P) (z : Euclid P), (∀ k, zs k ∈ ball (0 : Euclid P) 1 ∩ sing (φs k)) → Tendsto zs atTop (𝓝 z) → z ∈ sing ψ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma T of the parent proof (step 1), in the general form used in parent steps 4, 8 and 9. Simon, proof of A.4, chapter-A.txt line 135 ('sing ψ ≠ ∅ (by A.3(3))') and lines 150–151 ('{ξ/2} ⊆ sing ψ by A.3(2), (3)').
1. Let ε > 0. Apply A.3(3) to ψ ∈ F, the sequence φ_k ∈ F (which converges weakly to ψ) and ε/2. This gives k₀ such that for all k ≥ k₀, B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k ⊆ {w : ∃ v ∈ sing ψ, |w − v| < ε/2}.
2. Since z_k ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k, step 1 gives for every k ≥ k₀ a point v_k ∈ sing ψ with |z_k − v_k| < ε/2.
3. Since z_k → z, there is k₁ with |z_k − z| < ε/2 for all k ≥ k₁. For k := max(k₀, k₁), |z − v_k| ≤ |z − z_k| + |z_k − v_k| < ε. So for every ε > 0 the ball B_ε(z) meets sing ψ, i.e. z lies in the closure of sing ψ.
4. sing ψ is closed because ψ ∈ F (A.3c), so z ∈ sing ψ. ∎
proof_key_steps: A.3(3) with ε/2 places each z_k (k large) within ε/2 of a point of sing ψ
z_k → z places z within ε of sing ψ for every ε > 0
sing ψ is closed, hence z ∈ sing ψ

audit.reason: The type matches all stated hypotheses. Upper semicontinuity with ε/2 and convergence of the singular points place the limit in the closure of sing ψ; closedness proves membership. The argument also correctly excludes an empty limiting singular set.
